upstream.scope: Confirmed graceful termination of one process (D1 §§6.2, 7.7, 18.2, 27; D2 T24, T32; K2): --actions terminate adds Terminate…, which prepares an immutable intent and an inline confirmation panel of fresh, never-reused nodes (Row, Text, Button) bound to that intent; the panel's Confirm sends SIGTERM through ProcessActions to the one PidfdTerminator, which acquires a PX-029 handle at Confirm from its one table, checks key_of against the intent's key and settles it at once. Cancel, expiry, navigation (the server's resolved selection leaving the intent's process), read-only mode and identity replacement withdraw the intent and delete its panel. PID 1, --protect-pid PIDs and the server-derived support chain (srtop, its ancestors, each connected transport by socket peer PID and its ancestors) are refused, after the PX-028 owner, identity and freshness checks. Where PID file descriptors are unavailable Terminate… stays disabled with the reason and nothing falls back to kill(pid). Without --actions the package is unchanged and read-only. No protocol, registry, SDK, runtime, renderer or client change. Contributes to HTOP-R1-001 (owner PX-028/PX-031), which stays planned until PX-031 observes the outcome

entries.feature: Terminate… and a fresh confirmation panel per intent: --actions terminate labels Prepare 'Terminate…'; a prepared intent is shown in a panel (Row, Text naming the exact process and owner, Button 'Confirm: terminate PID n · name') whose three node IDs are PANEL_ID_BASE + 3n.. for the n-th intent of a run, never reused (§6.2), at most DEFAULT_CONFIRMATION_PANELS (4096) per run, then Prepare is refused; one Confirm handler per slot is registered at start (the runtime cannot remove a handler), and a slot's handler confirms only the intent shown in that slot; a consumed, cancelled or withdrawn intent's panel is deleted, so its Confirm names no node; PX-028's generic Confirm (node 85) is gone; repeated cycles leave the live node count, handler table and descriptors unchanged

entries.feature: Confirm sends SIGTERM to exactly the confirmed instance through the one production executor that can reach a process: PidfdTerminator holds one ProcessHandles table, acquires at Confirm (identity re-checked after pidfd_open), refuses a handle whose key_of is not the intent's key, settles it with HandleSignal::Terminate and closes it; a replaced PID is refused after the open and the newcomer receives nothing; Sent is reported as Requested ('SIGTERM was sent; the process may handle or ignore it, and whether it exits is not yet observed'), never as complete; a live test-owned worker that handles SIGTERM exits 0

entries.feature: Cancel, expiry, navigation, read-only mode and identity replacement invalidate the intent: navigation is the server's resolved selection no longer naming the intent's process instance (another row, a cleared selection, or a filter, search or view change that moves it); Confirm refuses a navigated intent (Refusal::Navigated) and ActionGate::revalidate, run on every selection change, republication and sample, withdraws an expired, navigated or no-longer-eligible intent and deletes its panel; prepare A, select B, confirm: A's intent is rejected and nothing is opened or sent; a paused or resuming view holds the intent with Confirm disabled; cancelled and expired intents never reach the executor

entries.feature: Protected targets: PID 1 and --protect-pid PIDs (repeatable, at most 64, only with --actions) in every source; for this host's live processes the support chain the server derives from its own process tree and connections, never from a client: srtop itself and its ancestors (/proc/<pid>/stat parents), each connected client's transport (the socket peer PID, the srui-ssh-bridge) and its ancestors (the SSH session); an unreadable chain refuses every live target; checked after the owner, identity and freshness checks, at Prepare, Confirm and revalidation

entries.feature: PX-008's audit, adjusted minimally: src/terminate.rs alone besides src/handle.rs may name the handle module, and only ProcessHandles, HandleSignal, SignalOutcome, AcquireError and HandleId (not the system-call seam); production holds exactly one handle table construction (ProcessHandles::live() in src/terminate.rs), exactly one settlement (.settle(id, HandleSignal::Terminate) there) and one PidfdTerminator::live() in src/main.rs; the production ProcessActions are exactly DryRunExecutor (src/actions.rs) and PidfdTerminator (src/terminate.rs); kill, libc, unsafe and syscall stay refused outside src/handle.rs, the only system-call site; the panels' Confirm handlers are allowed only as on(panel_confirm, ACTIVATE, ..) in src/lib.rs
